The test contains multiple, meaningful assertions (equality between graphs, equality to expected default, and a relational assertion >=1). This verifies multiple properties of the result and increases fault detection capability.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out tests in the method. Test is active and runnable per decision rule 3.
No requirement traceability annotations or Javadoc are present in the method itself (no @Story, @Requirement, or REQ- IDs). Decision rules 1-3 find no traceability information in method code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout parameter (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related guard. Decision rule 2 makes this compliant when such timing assertions are present.
The method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. Decision rule 2 flags generic names as non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: No clear signs of heavy code generation (no auto-generated comments or repetitive generated test names in the method). Per decision rules, mark as not-applicable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains Given-When-Then style comments that indicate design intent (Given/When/Then). Decision rule 1 recognizes this as evidence of thoughtful design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices()) and does not use reflection or inspect private state. Decision rules 1-3 indicate compliance.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages and use specific assertion methods (assertEquals, assertTrue) rather than generic assertTrue alone. Decision rules indicate compliance.
The test uses concise Given-When-Then comments that explain intent without excessive commenting. There is no commented-out code. Decision rules 1 and 3 indicate compliance.
The test uses no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no time-based calls, no Thread.sleep). It uses local state only, so decision rules indicate deterministic design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local variables, does not persist data or modify static state, and does not perform I/O. Decision rule 3 indicates the test is side-effect free.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: No per-method categorization annotations (@Tag/@Category) are present on the method itself. Decision rule 3 marks absence of method-level labels as non-compliant (we only inspect the method code).
